learningObjective: Reason about the throughput vs latency trade-off in LLM serving and identify how batch size affects each metric.

canonicalClaims.claim: Increasing batch size amortizes weight-HBM reads across more requests (raising throughput) but raises per-step wall time (raising per-request TPOT); beyond a threshold the workload transitions from bandwidth-bound to compute-bound with diminishing returns.
conditions: Fixed hardware; batch size is the tuning knob.
nonImplications: Does not imply the trade-off is linear.
Does not imply the optimum is universal across SLA classes.

misconceptions.claim: Latency and throughput are inverses (1/latency = throughput).
misconceptions.whyWrong: Throughput is aggregate; latency is per-request. Batching separates them.

misconceptions.claim: Increasing batch has no downside beyond memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-request TPOT increases with batch size; SLA can fail.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous batching removes the throughput-latency trade-off.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Continuous batching improves scheduling; the fundamental trade-off remains.

implementationFacts: TRT-LLM and vLLM benchmarks routinely show sub-linear throughput scaling past a certain batch size.
SLA-based auto-scaling picks batch to meet TPOT budget while maximizing aggregate throughput.
performanceScenarios: Chatbot workloads prefer smaller batches for low TPOT; batch inference workloads (offline generation) prefer larger batches.
